transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-19
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~46 min
- Attendees: Maya Patel, Ethan Cole (Redwood) — Janet Liu, Ravi Desai, Omar Ahmed (Calmwater)

Summary: 
Janet asked for a security intake covering SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit log retention/export, KMS/HSM options, and data residency. Redwood AE/SE walked through hosted vs dedicated vs private options with emphasis on audit trail, key management, and retention/deletion controls. Action items and benchmarking plan agreed.

Topics: SOC2 vs ISO, SAML/SSO + SCIM, RBAC model, audit logs & SIEM integration, KMS & HSM, data retention/delete API, hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs, network egress and VPC peering.

Artifacts referenced:
- Redwood SOC2/ISO packet: https://redwood.internal/soc2-iso-2026.pdf
- KMS integration guide (sample): https://docs.redwood.ai/kms-integration
- Benchmark template spreadsheet: https://slack-redwood/shared/benchmarks/Calmwater-template

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, really quick intro — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, with Ethan, our solutions engineer.
[00:00:12] Ethan Cole: Hi all, glad to be here. We'll walk through security posture questions first and then talk deployment paths.
[00:00:22] Janet Liu: Thanks, quick context — Calmwater's building an underwriting assistant that touches PII and health-adjacent claims. We're evaluating options because we need strict controls on keys, logs, and retention. SOC2 Type II is a must, ISO 27001 preferred.
[00:00:40] Ravi Desai: And we have an internal SAML SSO (Okta), SCIM provision, and we need RBAC that maps to our AD groups. Also need audit logs forwarded to Splunk.
[00:00:52] Omar Ahmed: Latency targets are 150ms p99 for short prompts; cost matters but second to compliance.
[00:00:59] Maya Patel: Great, that's clear. To be explicit, we can serve you three ways — Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated clusters (reserved GPU pools), or Private (VPC/on-prem). Each has tradeoffs for keys and logs.
[00:01:15] Ethan Cole: Quick note on terminology — our runtime does KV cache and continuous batching, though sometimes the transcript tool writes K-C cache, apologies.
[00:01:26] Janet Liu: Haha, no worries. For Hosted — can we bring our own keys? and does Redwood see plaintext?
[00:01:34] Maya Patel: For Hosted, by default keys are managed by Redwood KMS, and data is encrypted at rest. If you require customer-managed keys, we offer a BYOK flow that uses your cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP, Azure Key Vault). We also support an HSM-backed option via partner HSM for Private/Dedicated in enterprise deals.
[00:01:56] Ravi Desai: So Hosted + BYOK means Redwood still touches ciphertext for processing, correct? How do you ensure keys aren't exfiltrated?
[00:02:05] Ethan Cole: Correct that we decrypt in the serving layer to run inference. We isolate decryption in a hardened enclave within the dedicated runtime; access to KMS is scoped by IAM roles and audited. For additional assurance, our Private deployment can be configured so keys never leave your VPC — either remote key wrapping with your KMS or HSM in your network.
[00:02:29] Janet Liu: Ok. For SOC2 evidence, do you provide SOC2 Type II and ISO reports?
[00:02:36] Maya Patel: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestations — I'll send the redacted reports after this call. See link in artifacts.
[00:02:44] Omar Ahmed: What's the retention window for audit logs and how are they exported? We need logs forwarded to Splunk for at least 7 years for certain claims workflows.
[00:02:53] Ethan Cole: We retain operational audit logs by default for 90 days in the console but we provide a log export/snapshot pipeline to push logs to customer SIEMs — S3 export, direct syslog, or using our Splunk HEC integration. For long-term archival (years) customers typically route logs to their own S3 buckets; Redwood supports automated lifecycle policies to stream logs continuously.
[00:03:17] Ravi Desai: Does the exported audit log include request/response payloads? We cannot export PII or full responses for privacy.
[00:03:24] Maya Patel: Good point. Audit logs include metadata (request id, model, token counts, user id, time, route) by default. Payload redaction is supported: you can configure to omit or mask response bodies and PII fields before export. We can also provide hashed identifiers instead of raw values.
[00:03:42] Janet Liu: That matters. We need the ability to purge data on demand for particular users — a deletion API.
[00:03:48] Ethan Cole: We have a delete API and retention controls per project/route. For Hosted customers we support soft-deletes and a purge workflow; for Dedicated/Private you get control to run immediate purges inside your environment. We'll send the delete API spec.
[00:04:02] Omar Ahmed: Can we get field-level encryption? we prefer that the sensitive fields be encrypted client-side.
[00:04:09] Maya Patel: Yes, client-side field encryption is an approach customers use. Redwood supports tokenization patterns and can accept already-encrypted payloads — the model works on ciphertext if you orchestrate a de-tokenization step in pre/post processing in your stack. We also have examples for envelope encryption using your KMS.
[00:04:26] [00:04:27] Janet Liu: About RBAC — we need role mappings from Okta groups and least privilege, e.g., only certain teams can run production routes.
[00:04:34] Ethan Cole: We provide RBAC with role templates (admin, developer, auditor) and support SCIM for SCIM-enabled IdPs to sync groups. For Dedicated/Private you can even enforce network-level ACLs so only specific subnets can call the inference endpoints.
[00:04:49] Ravi Desai: Any ability to lock down model versions and prevent users from switching models? We need immutable production endpoints.
[00:04:56] Maya Patel: Yes, you can pin model versions and lock rollout policies. We also have an approvals workflow for model rollouts — changes require an approver and are logged in the audit trail.
[00:05:06] Omar Ahmed: About data residency — we need EU-only processing for certain customers. How granular are region controls?
[00:05:13] Ethan Cole: We have region-level routing: you can force requests to an EU region. For Hosted, we offer regional hosting. For Private, obviously you control placement. We also sign DTSAs and offer data processing addenda.
[00:05:25] Janet Liu: On encryption: do you support envelope encryption and key rotation?
[00:05:29] Maya Patel: Yes, envelope encryption with customer KMS and rotating keys with automatic rewrap is supported. We publish key rotation windows and can coordinate rotations with your security team.
[00:05:39] Ravi Desai: About network connectivity — if we do Dedicated in our VPC, is there direct peering or do you do VPN?
[00:05:46] Ethan Cole: Options: VPC peering or private interconnects for major cloud providers; for smaller setups we use customer-managed VPNs. For Private deployments you can deploy the control plane in your environment and avoid cross-cloud traffic.
[00:05:58] Janet Liu: Are there restrictions on model quantization or change in fidelity for compliance? I.e., sometimes quantized models behave oddly and we need to ensure no quality regression.
[00:06:08] Ethan Cole: Good question. Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per workload and we tie quality monitoring to prompt sets/evals. For production-critical routes we recommend dedicated instances with validated quantization profiles and we can run A/B test rollouts with automatic rollback on regression.
[00:06:24] [00:06:25] Omar Ahmed: What about third-party audits? Have you had penetration tests and will you share scope?
[00:06:30] Maya Patel: Yes, we run annual pentests and vuln scans — I can provide redacted reports and scope. We'll also include our bug-bounty summary.
[00:06:39] Ravi Desai: On SSO: Do you support Just-In-Time provisioning and session lifetime controls?
[00:06:44] Ethan Cole: Yes, session lifetimes, SAML attributes mapping, and JIT provisioning via SCIM/SCIM delta sync are supported.
[00:06:53] Janet Liu: Ok. A few edge questions — can we do model tracing per request for reproducibility? like capture random seeds, model config.
[00:07:01] Maya Patel: We log model config, model version, sampling parameters, and request id. We have a trace view in the console and can export traces for offline reproducibility.
[00:07:11] [00:07:12] Omar Ahmed: If a court order asks for data, what's the process?
[00:07:17] Ethan Cole: For Hosted we follow customer notification procedures per our DPA and will work through legal — we don't disclose customer content except per court order and we notify unless constrained. For Private deployments, you manage that entirely.
[00:07:29] Janet Liu: Any limits on export of embeddings — we use embeddings for similarity search and want to store them separately.
[00:07:36] Maya Patel: No problem — embeddings can be streamed out and you control storage lifecycle. We can optionally hash embeddings before export if you want to avoid raw vectors leaving the runtime.
[00:07:46] Ravi Desai: For the benchmark run — can we include our anonymized claims dataset?
[00:07:51] Ethan Cole: Yes, we recommend you anonymize PII if running on Hosted; for Dedicated/Private we can run on full data within your VPC. We'll provide a guide for what needs to be redacted for Hosted runs.
[00:08:03] Janet Liu: How are secrets rotated for service accounts?
[00:08:07] Maya Patel: We support short-lived service tokens, KMS-backed service keys, and integration with your secret manager via IAM roles. Session tokens can be rotated automatically.
[00:08:18] Omar Ahmed: One concern — audit log tampering. Who has the ability to delete or edit logs?
[00:08:24] Ethan Cole: Logs are immutable in the primary store for a default retention window; only designated compliance roles can request exports or redaction requests through a tracked workflow. For Dedicated/Private, you can define stricter immutability with WORM storage.
[00:08:39] Janet Liu: Great. Can you outline the difference in SLA and SLO between Hosted and Dedicated?
[00:08:45] Maya Patel: Hosted has a standard uptime SLA for paid tiers; Dedicated includes SLA-backed latency and throughput with reserved capacity. We'll include the SLA matrix in the follow-up packet.
[00:08:56] Ravi Desai: From a procurement perspective we may want an enterprise contract with on-prem option eventually.
[00:09:01] Maya Patel: Understood; we can scope Private deployment options during procurement.
[00:09:05] Janet Liu: Anything we should know about data deletion certs?
[00:09:09] Ethan Cole: We can provide deletion certificates after purge for Hosted customers. For Dedicated/Private you can run provable deletion within your environment.
[00:09:19] [00:09:20] Omar Ahmed: Could you email over the KMS integration example and the delete API?
[00:09:23] Maya Patel: Yes, I'll include both; Ethan will include the benchmark steps.
[00:09:27] 
[00:09:40] -- Mid-call clarification and brief demo outline --
[00:09:40] Maya Patel: Quick demo later would show the console trace, audit view, and how to pin models. We won't demo with PII.
[00:09:50] Ethan Cole: For the benchmark we'll set up two runs: hosted with redaction rules and dedicated in a sandbox VPC with full data. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost, and quality metrics on the same prompts.
[00:10:03] Janet Liu: Sounds good. About encryption at rest for object stores of embeddings and logs — are they encrypted with customer keys?
[00:10:10] Ethan Cole: We can configure object stores to use customer-managed keys; otherwise Redwood-managed keys are used. That applies to embeddings, logs, and snapshots.
[00:10:20] Ravi Desai: Are there any parts of the stack where plaintext hits log files inadvertently? We've seen other vendors log request bodies in debug mode.
[00:10:27] Maya Patel: We avoid logging full request bodies in production. Debug-level capture is off by default and requires an explicit opt-in by admin and is recorded in an approval flow.
[00:10:37] Janet Liu: Onboarding timeline — if we choose Dedicated, how long to provision?
[00:10:42] Ethan Cole: Provisioning timeline depends on capacity, but typical Dedicated onboarding is 4–6 weeks (contract + infra), Private on-prem is longer. Hosted is immediate.
[00:10:52] Omar Ahmed: Any compliance connectors for PCI or HIPAA?
[00:10:56] Maya Patel: We have a HIPAA addendum and can sign BAAs; PCI is more scoped but we can discuss specific controls.
[00:11:05] Ravi Desai: Ok, let's capture some of these as concrete requirements from our side.
[00:11:10] Janet Liu: Must-have list: SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 certs, BYOK (AWS KMS) support, SCIM + SAML, Splunk forwarding, deletion API + deletion certificates, EU region processing, RBAC mirroring AD groups, immutable audit logs or WORM archival.
[00:11:31] Ethan Cole: Noted. We'll map capabilities to Hosted/Dedicated/Private in the follow-up. For some items like WORM and HSM we typically recommend Dedicated or Private.
[00:11:41] Maya Patel: We'll also provide suggested network diagrams for VPC peering and private endpoints.
[00:11:47] 
[00:12:05] -- Closing section with explicit next steps --
[00:12:05] Maya Patel: To recap next steps — I'll send attestation docs, Ethan will set up the benchmark, and Ravi will supply data retention and sample anonymized dataset. We'll sync week of Nov 30 for the benchmark start.
[00:12:20] Janet Liu: That works. One last thing — can we get a demo account so our platform team can poke around?
[00:12:27] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll provision a read-only demo org and a sandbox project.
[00:12:33] Omar Ahmed: Great, thanks.
[00:12:35] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email and share links.

-- End of recorded extract --
